lines.trans: For fifteen years in my hands, that board only held hooks one through eight.
And look on the right edge—there were two tiny screw holes under the varnish all along.
No way! Hook number nine used to hang right there thirty years ago!
One turn, two turns... solid brass hook number nine, back where it belongs.
May I hang the big sunroom key on it, Tariq?
Go right ahead, Nour. You earned it this week.
Wait—Tariq, what is that laminated card tucked inside your paper ledger?
Aha! Did you secretly keep a copy of my printed café menu, Tariq?!
Only because your big numbers are easy to read without a lamp.
Write this day down in the guest book: Tariq praised a printed page!
Don't celebrate too much, boss. Paper books still win when it rains.
Look at the courtyard clock—half past five! Let us light the lanterns!

Goodbye!

meanings.note: Exclamation when a puzzle clicks into place ('aha!').

examples.trans: Aha! Now I understand the whole story!
Aha, that is why you took the bus!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: أصلية, plural: أصليين).

examples.trans: The ceiling is solid oak wood.
All the old tilework is original.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb taking بـ for what is celebrated.

examples.text: رح نحتفل بافتتاح الكافيه مع كل الجيران.
examples.trans: We're going to celebrate the café opening with all the neighbours.

examples.text: احتفلنا لما خلص دهان الشيش قبل المغرب.
examples.trans: We celebrated when the shutter painting finished before dusk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian Form X verb (بيستاهل / بتستاهل) meaning 'to deserve, be worth it'.

examples.trans: The ovens deserve a break after baking!

examples.text: انتي بتستاهلي كل خير يا سلمى.
examples.trans: You deserve every good thing, Salma.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Passive Levantine Arabic verb from قرا ('to read'), meaning 'to be readable'.

examples.text: الخط كتير صغير لدرجة إنه ما بينقرأ من بعيد.
examples.trans: The handwriting is so small that it can't be read from a distance.
The letter was read aloud in front of everyone at the celebration.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'without', used identically to MSA.

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word (from Turkish burgu) for a metal screw.

examples.trans: I tightened the screw with the small screwdriver.
The chair needs a new screw.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Singular form for any type of card (ID, credit, ticket, etc.).

examples.trans: There is a paper tag on the suitcase.
I wrote my name on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

تفضّل.gloss: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Feminine noun for the rim of a tin or the edge of a paving stone (الحافة الشمالية 'the north edge'). Plural: حواف.

examples.trans: We wrapped white tape around the rim of the tin.
Lower the north edge first gently.

meanings.note: The number five, used in counting abstractly or before masculine counted nouns.

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'fifteen' before a counted noun (خمستعشر سنة 'fifteen years').

examples.trans: I have not seen it in fifteen years!
The landing is after fifteen steps.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Feminine noun used in Jordanian weather expressions: الدنيا بتمطر ('it is raining'), الدنيا برد ('it is cold out').

examples.trans: It is raining outside right now.
It is sunny and lovely out this morning.

رجع.gloss: to return; come back; start again

meanings.en: to return; come back; start again
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجع, بيرجع).

examples.trans: Can you run there and come back in ten minutes?
Did the pipe start dripping again?

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسرار.

examples.trans: Rest assured, your secret is safe with us.

examples.text: سر الكيكة الزاكية هو الليمون الطازج.
examples.trans: The secret to tasty cake is fresh lemon.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'easy to do'.

examples.text: هاي الوصفة سهلة وبتجهز بنص ساعة.
examples.trans: This recipe is easy and comes together in half an hour.

examples.text: سهل نرتب الكراسي بعد ما يخلص الدهان.
examples.trans: It will be easy to arrange the chairs once the painting is done.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Levantine Arabic verb for 'to rain', derived from شتا ('winter/rain').

examples.text: الدنيا عم بتشتّي برا، خد معك شمسية!
examples.trans: It's raining outside—take an umbrella with you!

examples.text: تشرين الثاني بلّش تشتّي فيه بغزارة بعمان.
examples.trans: In November it started raining heavily in Amman.

meanings.note: Traditional Levantine word for an iron hook-and-eye latch on wooden shutters or doors.

examples.text: رفعنا شنكل الحديد ففتح الشيش فورا.
examples.trans: We lifted the iron hook latch and the shutter swung right open.

examples.text: سكر شنكل الشباك منيح قبل ما تنام.
examples.trans: Fasten the window latch securely before going to sleep.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صفحات.

examples.trans: Read the second page of the letter.
The notebook fell open to the middle page.

ضوّى.gloss: to light up; shine; switch on a light

meanings.en: to light up; shine; switch on a light
meanings.note: Used for a lamp that glows and for the person who switches it on (ضوي الضو 'turn on the light').

examples.trans: The new lamp gives good light.
Turn the light on, the room is dark.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: ضيفة). Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Male given name of the veteran handyman.

examples.text: المعلم طارق صلّح الحنفية والمفصلات بنص ساعة.
examples.trans: Master Tariq fixed the faucet and the hinges in half an hour.

examples.text: اسأل عمي طارق إذا معه المفك الكبير.
examples.trans: Ask Uncle Tariq if he has the big screwdriver with him.

طلع.gloss: to go up; go out; come out; turn out

meanings.en: to go up; go out; come out; turn out
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلع, بيطلع).

examples.text: لفائف القرفة هلا طلعت من الفرن!
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven!
Go up the stairs to the third floor.

meanings.note: Can refer to physical length, height, or duration of time (e.g., all day).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعلق, بيعلق).

examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror?
We hung the lanterns in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: After negation, ما ... غير means 'only / nothing except'.

examples.text: ما معي غير المعطف اللي علي!
examples.trans: I have nothing with me except the coat I have on!
There are only two valves on the shelf.

meanings.note: Feminine verb agreeing with non-human plural الدفاتر, from فاز ('to win').

examples.text: فريقنا فاز بالمباراة النهائية باللحظة الأخيرة!
examples.trans: Our team won the final match at the last moment!

examples.text: الدفاتر المرسومة بإيدهم فازت بالجائزة الأولى.
examples.trans: The notebooks they drew by hand won first prize.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun; فتحة قفل means 'keyhole'. Plural: فتحات.

examples.trans: There is a small keyhole on the front.
Air is coming through the window opening.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: A written list or a restaurant menu; with -i it is قائمتي, 'my list'.

examples.trans: I wrote the shopping list before the market.
May I have the menu?

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Refers to the material glass, a pane of glass, or sometimes a glass bottle.

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: Depending on vowels, it means 'he wrote' (katab) or plural 'books' (kutub).

examples.text: رح يكتب تقييم حلو عن النزل.
examples.trans: He will write a lovely review of the guesthouse.
I wrote my name and number on the card.

meanings.note: Placed AFTER the adjective or verb it intensifies: تقيلة كتير ('very heavy'), شكرا كتير ('thank you very much').

examples.trans: The smell is so good!
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'no' or 'not', used exactly like Standard Arabic.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Very common Jordanian word to indicate that an action is ongoing or hasn't happened yet.

examples.trans: Is your cup still intact?
Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: Used in Jordan to mean a wrap or a sandwich (e.g. falafel or shawarma), or a turn in the road.

examples.text: أكلت لفة قرفة سخنة مع الشاي.
examples.trans: I ate a warm cinnamon roll with tea.
Watch the tight turn on the stairs.

meanings.note: Common conjunction used to introduce a time clause, distinct from the question word 'when' (mita).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لمبات.

examples.trans: I fitted a new bulb in the attic bathroom.
The white lightbulb is bright.

meanings.note: Refers to a whiteboard (اللوح الأبيض), wooden plank, or windowpane (لوح قزاز).

examples.text: كتبنا مهام الأسبوع التلاتة عاللوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: We wrote the three tasks for the week on the whiteboard.

examples.text: نضفنا كل ألواح القزاز من الغبرة القديمة.
examples.trans: We cleaned all the glass panes of their old dust.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Passive participle indicating that an object has been set down or positioned somewhere.

examples.trans: The book is placed here.
The items are placed.

meanings.note: Masculine participle from خبّى ('to hide/keep away').

examples.text: حاسس إنك مخبّي عني خبر حلو، احكي شو في!
examples.trans: I feel like you're hiding good news from me—tell me what's up!

examples.text: طارق مخبّي المفاتيح الاحتياطية بالدرج التاني.
examples.trans: Tariq keeps the spare keys tucked away in the second drawer.

meanings.note: Sound Form I verb (بمدح / مدحت) from root م-د-ح, used when admiring someone's work or cooking.

examples.trans: Everyone praises you at the restaurant.
The guests praised the Arabic coffee.

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: Feminine participle from طبع ('to print'), agreeing with قائمة ('menu').

examples.text: القائمة المطبوعة الجديدة عليها كل أسعار المشروبات.
examples.trans: The new printed menu has all the drink prices on it.

examples.text: معي نسخة مطبوعة من العقد عشان نراجعها سوا.
examples.trans: I have a printed copy of the contract so we can review it together.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Standalone معقول! is a classic Jordanian exclamation of amazed disbelief ('No way! / Could it really be?!').

examples.text: معقول! قطار جدي الخشب لسا موجود!
examples.trans: Could it be! Grandfather's wooden train is still around!
The price is reasonable and fair for everyone.

meanings.note: Masculine participle from علّق ('to hang'), meaning 'hung up' or 'hanging'.

examples.text: البرواز القديم معلّق عالحيط فوق البيانو.
examples.trans: The old frame is hanging on the wall above the piano.

examples.text: المعطف معلّق ورا الباب عشان ما ينسى ياخده معه.
examples.trans: The coat is hung behind the door so he doesn't forget to take it with him.

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, يا معلم is an affectionate respectful title meaning 'boss'.

examples.text: يسلمو إيديك يا معلّم طارق، الشغل طلع فخم!
examples.trans: Bless your hands, Master Tariq—the work turned out top-notch!

examples.text: المعلّم بالورشة بعرف يصلّح أي عطل بالخشب.
examples.trans: The master craftsman at the workshop knows how to fix any wood damage.

meanings.note: Feminine participle meaning 'coated/wrapped' or 'laminated' in everyday Arabic.

examples.text: القائمة المطبوعة مغلّفة بالبلاستيك عشان ما تتوسخ.
examples.trans: The printed menu is laminated in plastic so it doesn't get dirty.

examples.text: الهدية جاهزة ومغلّفة بورق ملون وشريطة.
examples.trans: The gift is ready and wrapped in colored paper and a ribbon.

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Formal/signboard Arabic word for 'café' (alongside conversational كافيه), ideal for painted signs.

examples.text: كتبنا عاللوحة: مقهى جنينة الغرفة تسعة.
examples.trans: We painted on the sign: Room Nine Garden Café.

examples.text: المقهى رح يفتح يوميا من الصبح للمسا.
examples.trans: The café will be open daily from morning till evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أماكن.

examples.trans: This place is very quiet and comfortable.
Everything is tidy in its proper place.

meanings.note: Used to ask for permission 'is it possible?' or to say 'perhaps'.

examples.trans: May I see the room first?
Could I see the tag in the sunlight?

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from نسخ ('to copy'); used for photocopies, spare keys, or book editions. Plural: نسخ.

examples.trans: There's a second copy inside the house.
Make me a copy of the key.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Standard adverb for physical location.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Masculine word formed from ورق ('paper'), meaning 'made of paper'.

examples.text: نستخدم أكياس ورقية بدل البلاستيك بالمخبز.
examples.trans: We use paper bags instead of plastic at the bakery.

examples.text: لسه بفضل القراءة من كتاب ورقي أكتر من الشاشة.
examples.trans: I still prefer reading from a paper book rather than a screen.

meanings.note: Masculine singular loanword for wood varnish, with the Arabic definite article.

examples.text: دهنا الطاولات بالورنيش عشان تلمع وتحمي الخشب.
examples.trans: We coated the tables with varnish so they shine and protect the wood.

examples.text: ريحة الورنيش لسه قوية بالغرفة، افتح الشبابيك.
examples.trans: The smell of the varnish is still strong in the room—open the windows.

meanings.note: General term for time or duration.

examples.trans: Old pipes take time to warm up.
You arrived right on time.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Very common interjection used to urge action or to say goodbye ('yalla bye').

examples.trans: Come on, let us bring the bag down into the light!
Let us go check out the room right now!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
